title: Eight New K-Dramas Arriving in August 2026, From Our Sticky Love to Mousetrap
excerpt: Netflix leads a packed month with Jung Hae-In's amnesia romance and Ryu Jun-Yeol's identity-theft thriller, while tvN and SBS fill the schedule with music dramas, office comedies, and crime sequels.
body:
• Netflix drops Our Sticky Love on August 7, starring Jung Hae-In and Ha Young in a 12-episode amnesia romance, with all episodes available at once.
  • Song Kang returns to the screen after military service in Four Hands, Two Sonatas, a classical-music drama premiering August 29 on tvN.
  • Webtoon adaptation Mousetrap, starring Ryu Jun-Yeol and Sul Kyung-Gu, is expected on Netflix around August 18, though the date is not yet confirmed.
  • SBS brings back Flex x Cop for a second season starting August 7, while tvN's office romcom My Bias, My Boss premieres the same week.

August 2026 shapes up as one of the most loaded K-drama months of the year, with at least eight new series spanning romantic comedy, psychological thriller, classical music, and revenge melodrama across Netflix, tvN, SBS, and KBS. Here is a guide to every major premiere and what makes each one worth watching.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Wndx_3B0lgc

The Netflix Headliners

Our Sticky Love, the month's most anticipated premiere, lands on Netflix on August 7 with all 12 episodes dropping at once. Jung Hae-In plays Jang Tae-ha, a former youth boxing champion turned coach in a rural village who recognizes the woman who just lost her memory as his first love. Ha Young stars as Go Eun-sae, a sharp Seoul prosecutor who wakes up after an accident with no recollection of her identity. To shield her from a dangerous crime boss played by Heo Sung-tae, Tae-ha tells a calculated lie — claiming to be her boyfriend. According to What's on Netflix, fans are "looking forward to watching the effortless chemistry between Jung Hae In and Ha Young unfold."

Later in the month, Netflix is expected to release Mousetrap, one of the year's most anticipated thrillers. Adapted from Ludvico's popular webtoon, the series stars Ryu Jun-yeol as Je Mun-jae, a reclusive novelist with severe social phobia whose quiet existence unravels when a mysterious figure known as "The Rat" steals his identity, name, and fortune. Sul Kyung-gu plays a ruthless loan shark and private detective who agrees to help track down the imposter. Director Kim Hong-seon helms the project. An August 18 release date has been widely reported but remains unconfirmed.

"To shield her from a dangerous crime boss played by Heo Sung-tae, Tae-ha tells a calculated lie — claiming to be her boyfriend."

Four Hands, Two Sonatas rounds out the Netflix slate on August 29. The 12-episode music romance marks Song Kang's return to the screen after completing his mandatory military service — a homecoming that has generated significant buzz among the Korean actor's global fanbase. Set at a prestigious arts high school, the series follows piano prodigy Kang Bi-o (Song Kang) whose trajectory is disrupted by the arrival of Choi Jeong-yo (Lee Jun-young), a gifted rival who abandoned his talent after personal tragedy. Jang Gyu-ri co-stars as a viola major who connects the two musicians. The show airs on tvN domestically and streams on Netflix internationally.

Broadcast Premieres Filling the Schedule

My Bias, My Boss kicks off the month on August 3 on tvN. Based on a popular webcomic, the office romantic comedy follows Nam Da-reum (Kim Hye-jun), who has spent 11 years as a devoted fan of idol-turned-director Lee Chan (Cha Woo-min). She turns down corporate offers to join his fashion startup, only to clash with Kang Ha-ki (Kang Hoon), the company's reserved CEO. New episodes air Mondays and Tuesdays.

Flex x Cop 2 brings the chaebol-detective franchise back to SBS on August 7. Ahn Bo-hyun returns as Jin I-soo, who solves high-profile cases using his vast wealth, but faces a new adversary in strict team leader Joo Hye-ra (Jung Eun-chae). The 14-episode second season airs Fridays and Saturdays.

KBS launches A Trap Called Desire on August 10, a 100-episode daily revenge melodrama. Veteran actress Jang Seo-hee returns to KBS primetime as Joo Mi-ran, a ruthless woman who frames Go Eun-seol (Jeon Hye-won) for murder to steal her life. The series airs weekdays at 7:50 PM KST.

ENA rounds out the month with New Recruit Season 4, returning August 24 for an 8-episode run on Studio Genie.

Continuing Series Worth Catching Up On

Two ongoing Netflix series carry momentum into August. The Apartment Job, a JTBC crime-comedy starring Ji Sung as a former gangster who accidentally becomes a local hero while running for apartment council president, reaches its finale around August 16. And Spooky in Love, Park Eun-bin's occult romance about a hotel heiress who sees ghosts teaming up with a prosecutor played by Yang Se-jong, continues weekly after its July 18 premiere.

What Indian Viewers Should Know

For viewers in India and across the diaspora, the Netflix titles — Our Sticky Love, Mousetrap, and Four Hands, Two Sonatas — will be available with subtitles on the same day as their Korean premiere. India has emerged as one of Netflix's fastest-growing K-drama markets, with the Hallyu wave fueling dedicated online communities and fan events in cities from Mumbai to Bengaluru. Jung Hae-In already commands a strong Indian following after Snowdrop and Something in the Rain, making Our Sticky Love a likely trending title on Indian Netflix this month.

Looking Ahead

August's lineup reflects how far Korean drama has pushed beyond traditional romance. The month spans amnesia rom-coms, webtoon-adapted identity thrillers, classical music rivalries, and 100-episode revenge sagas. With Song Kang's military-service comeback and the potential arrival of Mousetrap, August could set the stage for the strongest fall season Korean television has seen in years.
